Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old male presents with several months of low mood, decreased appetite and energy, intermittent nausea, unintentional weight loss, and episodic palpitations/subjective shortness of breath (not associated with exertion), with history of treated hypothyroidism but currently off thyroxine.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Low mood, decreased appetite, low energy, intermittent nausea, unintentional weight loss, and episodes of palpitations/shortness of breath.
- Timeline:
  - Low mood, reduced appetite, low energy began approximately 3–3.5 months ago after changing law firm (patient stated).
  - Weight loss began earlier, approximately 6 months ago; patient estimates about one stone loss over that period.
  - Intermittent nausea “every now and again,” no vomiting.
  - Episodic palpitations/feeling short of breath occur most notably in elevators and in similar situations; patient can walk up to ~1 mile without shortness of breath.
  - Has not been taking levothyroxine since changing GP (timeframe not precisely documented); no recent blood tests.
- Exacerbating / relieving factors:
  - Palpitations/shortness of breath are triggered or occur notably in elevators/closed spaces; not consistently related to exertion.
  - Reduced physical activity recently; patient reports not walking much.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - Headaches and episodic nausea reported.
  - No chest pain with palpitations.
  - Bowel habits reported as normal: no diarrhea, no blood, no mucus, no vomiting.
  - Work functioning: can perform work but with some difficulties; patient is a lawyer and reports some trouble at work.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No vomiting, no diarrhea, no blood per rectum, no chest pain, no cough, no reflux reported.

Past Medical History:
- Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid).
  - Patient has taken levothyroxine in the past but reports he is not taking it currently; reason given: stopped after changing doctor. No recent thyroid function tests documented.
- No other medical conditions mentioned.

Medications:
- Levothyroxine — patient previously took; currently not taking. Dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No other medications documented.

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Social History:
- Age: 35-year-old male.
- Occupation: Lawyer.
- Lives with wife; patient noted wife has complained about “nightly activities” (no further detail).
- Physical activity: reduced recently; reports not walking much lately.
- Smoking, alcohol, recreational drug use: not documented.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination findings documented.
- Vital signs: not documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations completed during this encounter.
- Planned investigations per clinician:
  - "General set of bloods" including: full blood count (to assess for anemia), renal function, liver function, vitamin levels, and thyroid function tests (specific test names not documented).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Low mood, decreased appetite, low energy (possible depressive symptoms)
  - Assessment: Patient reports several months of low mood, low energy, reduced appetite, and functional impact at home and work; formal diagnosis not documented in transcript.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange general blood tests (see Investigations) to assess for reversible medical causes (anemia, metabolic, thyroid, vitamin deficiencies).
    - After blood results, clinician will review and consider further assessment including physical examination and mental health evaluation as appropriate.
    - Advise patient to contact services sooner if symptoms worsen.
- Issue 2: Episodic palpitations and subjective shortness of breath (not exertional; prominent in enclosed spaces)
  - Assessment: Patient describes palpitations and dyspnea particularly in elevators; can walk ~1 mile without dyspnea; no chest pain reported. No acute features documented.
  - Plan:
    - Include assessment of thyroid function and other relevant blood tests as above.
    - If chest pain, severe palpitations, syncope, or other acute cardiorespiratory symptoms occur: go to Emergency Department (A&E).
    - Reassess after blood results; consider further cardiopulmonary evaluation if symptoms persist or worsen (not specifically ordered in transcript).
- Issue 3: Known hypothyroidism with medication nonadherence
  - Assessment: Patient stopped levothyroxine after changing doctor; no recent blood tests to document thyroid status.
  - Plan:
    - Obtain thyroid function tests as part of the blood panel.
    - Review results and consider reinitiating or adjusting levothyroxine based on results and clinical assessment (specific changes to therapy not documented).
- General plan items:
  - Patient instructed to call the support number in the app (an 03xx number) to arrange the blood tests; clinician will complete the form to organize tests.
  - Patient will receive a text when results are available prompting booking of follow-up appointment.
  - Advice given to seek immediate care (A&E) for chest pain or if bowel symptoms or vomiting develop/ worsen.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, temperature, oxygen saturation) are not documented.
  - No formal mental health screening scores or suicide risk assessment documented.
  - No medication dose/route/frequency for levothyroxine documented.
  - No allergies recorded.
  - No physical examination documented.
  - No laboratory or imaging results available at time of consult.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Conflict noted between timing of decreased appetite (patient reports started ~3–3.5 months ago) and timing of weight loss (patient reports weight loss began earlier, approximately 6 months ago).
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Portions of the conversation had brief inaudible/uncertain segments; some patient responses were fragmented. Overall sufficient for history but physical exam and objective data are lacking.
